## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/_deprecations.py:75-91` currently marks eight environment/config aliases as `_permanent(...)` ergonomic renames: `REBAR_NO_SYNC`, `COMPACT_THRESHOLD`, `SCRATCH_BASE_DIR`, `REBAR_ACLI_TIMEOUT`, `RECONCILER_ABSENT_GET_BUDGET`, `REBAR_ID_GUARD_MODE`, `REBAR_VERIFY_OVERLAP_ENABLED`, and `verify.overlap_enabled`.

The Janitor approval record explicitly authorizes removal of every configuration alias. This ticket therefore intentionally reverses that prior permanent-alias classification as a pre-1.0 breaking change; it is not a claim that the existing scheduled-removal policy already applies. Because `REBAR_NO_SYNC` changes pull semantics and `REBAR_ID_GUARD_MODE` controls an unsafe bypass, silent fallback is unsafe.

## Approach

First record an ADR that supersedes permanent treatment for these eight aliases, cites the Janitor approval, names every canonical replacement, and chooses fail-loud migration rather than continued alias support. Replace each `_permanent` row with an `_tomb` entry at `error` behavior and a canonical replacement message; tombstones are deliberate removed-input detection, not a supported alias. Remove the matching active resolution/warning paths from `_config_sources.py`; remove `verify.overlap_enabled` from `_config_sections._ALIASES` (also surfaced through `_config_schema`) in the same change. Migrate every functional test consumer to canonical spelling, including `REBAR_NO_SYNC` consumers in `test_store_concurrency.py`, `test_next_batch_compute.py`, `test_bridge_preview_under_sync_contention_heldout.py`, and `test_read_freshness_parity.py`, plus `REBAR_ID_GUARD_MODE` consumers in `test_conflict_resolver_no_rebar_id_writes.py` and `test_rebar_id_label_writers.py`. Preserve canonical typed behavior and transformed semantics.

## Scope

- `docs/adr/` — new ADR recording the operator-approved permanent-to-removed reclassification and tombstone rationale.
- `src/rebar/_deprecations.py` — replace eight permanent alias declarations with error tombstones and canonical migration messages.
- `src/rebar/_config_sources.py` — delete active legacy env parsing/conversion/warning entries.
- `src/rebar/_config_sections.py` and its `_config_schema` consumer — remove `verify.overlap_enabled` alias enrollment.
- `tests/unit/test_config_surface_golden.py`, config tests, and the five named functional test consumers — migrate to canonical inputs and test tombstone failure.
- `docs/env-vars.md`, `docs/config.md`, `docs/config-reference.md`, `docs/bash-migration.md`, `docs/concurrency.md`, `docs/api-stability.md`, source docstrings, `CHANGELOG.md`, and release notes — replace live guidance with canonical names; retain only clearly dated historical records.

## Testing

For each of the eight removed spellings, prove config loading fails loudly with its canonical replacement in the error message; prove the canonical spelling parses to the same typed result. Cover the transformed `REBAR_NO_SYNC` inverse-pull and `REBAR_ID_GUARD_MODE=warn` unsafe-bypass boundaries through canonical fields, including the read-freshness opt-out parity path that currently parametrizes `REBAR_NO_SYNC`. Run a complete-population search for all eight tokens and classify every residual occurrence as exactly one of: a tombstone row/error test, the new ADR, or a clearly dated historical record; any live parser, warning, example, documentation, or functional-test consumer is a failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A new ADR records the explicit Janitor approval, the permanent-to-removed reclassification, all eight canonical replacements, and the fail-loud tombstone rationale.
- [ ] Each old env/config spelling is removed from active parsing and warning paths and is represented only by an `error` tombstone with a canonical migration message.
- [ ] `verify.overlap_enabled` is absent from both the deprecation registry and `_config_sections._ALIASES`/`_config_schema` enrollment.
- [ ] Every functional test consumer of the eight old spellings uses the canonical input instead.
- [ ] Tests prove each tombstone fails loudly and each canonical replacement retains its prior typed behavior, including the two transformed-value boundaries.
- [ ] The complete-population search finds no unclassified live alias reference; documentation and examples use only canonical spellings.
- [ ] Changelog/release documentation names every removal and canonical replacement.
